extracted.intended_audience: Early-stage investigators applying for NIH K01 mentored career development awards (and their mentors/reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation guidance and reviewer summary for an NIH K01 (Mentored Research Scientist Development Award) application, covering standard review criteria (Candidate, Career Development Plan, Research Plan, Mentors, Environment) and administrative requirements (human subjects, inclusion, resource sharing, budget).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact/Priority score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact/Priority score reflecting the likelihood that the application will have a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by assigned reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's qualifications, prior training, productivity, and potential to develop into an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include relevant field experience (e.g., time spent in-country), prior publications (first/co-first authorship), prior relevant projects (Fogarty fellowship, Global Burden of Disease work), leadership ability, creativity, quantitative training and skills, and letters of recommendation that speak to likelihood of independence. Reviewers note strengths (experience, collaborations, publications) or lack of weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals / Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the proposed training and mentoring plan to develop the candidate's skills and achieve career goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess alignment of training aims with scientific aims; clarity of mentor and team roles; coursework adequacy (data management, spatial epidemiology, modeling, data visualization, grant writing); practicability of didactic workload versus field work; realism of planned meeting frequency with mentors; and whether professional development (e.g., courses on writing proposals/manuscripts) is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific aims, methods, feasibility, and potential impact of the proposed research/training program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether aims are well-considered and revised as needed, feasibility given available data (vital registration, surveillance, DHIS-2, PEPFAR), appropriateness of modeling approaches (deterministic compartmental models, geospatial integration), plan for model validation, handling of co-factors (ART scale-up, INSTIs, drug resistance), incorporation of migration/urban–rural differences, and whether conditional aims (Aims 2 and 3) depend appropriately on validation of Aim 1. Consider feasibility of ambitious timelines and activities (e.g., stakeholder RCT) and risks such as slow accrual or secular changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentors, Co-Mentors, Consultants, Collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the mentorship team’s expertise, track record, and plan to mentor the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess mentor domain expertise (modeling, geospatial science, implementation science), history mentoring K awardees, letters of support, planned frequency and modality of meetings (weekly/in-person/Skype), clarity of roles for each mentor/advisor, and manageability of a large multidisciplinary, international team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of institutional resources, support, and commitment to the candidate’s success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider departmental, center, and institute resources (e.g., UW, ICRC, IHME, CFAR), connections with local partners (Ministry letters, National TB Program, CDC), feasibility of obtaining datasets, and explicit institutional commitments (e.g., planned faculty hire after fellowship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of protections for human subjects involved in the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether aims using existing data versus primary data collection are described with appropriate protections. Example: Aims 1 and 2 use existing models/data; Aim 3 is an implementation science RCT and requires consideration of risks, protections, and IRB. The document uses NIH coding (e.g., Code 30 ACCEPTABLE) and points reviewers to PHS398 and NIH human subjects policy guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to include a data and safety monitoring plan when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document notes 'NOT APPLICABLE' for DSM plan in this application, but generally reviewers check whether such a plan is appropriate for the proposed human subjects research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the research plan conforms to NIH policies on inclusion of women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH Code 1A ACCEPTABLE; projects must conform to policy and provide population details and rationale for inclusion/exclusion prior to undertaking studies; reviewers check that no one is excluded on the basis of sex without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Minorities Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the research plan conforms to NIH policies on inclusion of minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH Code 1A ACCEPTABLE; consider whether the study population reflects local demographics and that parameters are derived from underlying population data; no one should be excluded on the basis of race/ethnicity without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the research plan conforms to NIH policies on inclusion of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH Code 3A NOT APPLICABLE for this application; when applicable, details and rationale for inclusion/exclusion must be provided prior to studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with policies on humane care and use of vertebrate animals when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH Code 10 NOT APPLICABLE for this application; reviewers check protocols and compliance when vertebrate animals are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazard Comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of biohazard risks and appropriate containment plans when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked NOT APPLICABLE here, but reviewers would check for appropriate descriptions and safety measures if relevant biological hazards exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how well the applicant addressed weaknesses noted in prior submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers examine revisions (e.g., decreased coursework in Year 1, added deliverables, incorporation of migration, more model validation detail) and note whether prior critiques were thoughtfully considered and addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the RCR training plan for acceptability across format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, and frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application rated 'ACCEPTABLE' across subcomponents; reviewers expect a clear RCR plan meeting NIH expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Institution Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification for conducting research at a foreign site when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked JUSTIFIED here because the challenge (HIV–TB co-infection) is greatest in Sub-Saharan Africa and the work could not be conducted in the US. Reviewers check whether foreign setting is appropriate and necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (Data Sharing / Model/Data Accessibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for sharing data, model code, and other resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application marked ACCEPTABLE; when applicable, detailed data sharing plans (especially if >$500,000/year) and model/resource availability are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to address authentication of key biological/chemical resources when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section included; reviewers look for plans to authenticate key resources (not applicable for this proposal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether the requested budget and period of support are appropriate and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here the budget was recommended as requested and marked ACCEPTABLE; reviewers and grants management may adjust costs if award is planned. Administrative notes caution that shown budget has not been adjusted to reflect reviewer recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance / Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the study’s potential public health impact and relevance to the target population/field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary emphasizes that TB is the leading cause of death among PLHIV in Uganda and globally; reviewers evaluate whether the proposed tools (mapping/modeling) can stretch limited resources and guide prioritization of preventive therapy for maximal health impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility, Timeline, and Workload Balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether the proposed timeline and workload (didactic coursework, field work, meetings, clinical duties) are realistic and feasible within the project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers flagged concerns about heavy didactic work in Year 1 conflicting with field work, unrealistic weekly meetings with mentors, ambitious training plus travel, and whether stakeholder recruitment and trial timelines are achievable within four years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling-Specific Methodological Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of modeling methods, parameterization, data sources, validation, and assumptions used in geospatial and mathematical models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers examine use of vital registration, surveillance, DHIS-2, PEPFAR data; whether deterministic compartmental models and geospatial approaches are appropriate; inclusion of ART coverage, travel for care seeking, migration, rural–urban differences, drug resistance, INSTI rollout, availability of molecular epidemiology data, and plans for validation of model outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder Engagement and Implementation Science Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to engage stakeholders, measure acceptability/feasibility, and evaluate effect of presentation formats on uptake of model results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 3 evaluated for novelty and feasibility: use of stakeholder interviews, a trial of presentation formats (interactive 'gamification' vs passive lecture), outcomes (acceptability, feasibility, uptake), challenges in recruiting senior program leaders, and potential ethical/employment risks for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness and Economic Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for cost-effectiveness analysis and the inclusion of micro-costing data for intervention comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note added details on costing approaches and sources; mentor expertise in cost-effectiveness is a strength. Consider reduced efficacy in context of drug-resistant TB and inclusion of prevention strategies like 3HP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support and Mentor Track Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of letters of support and mentors’ history of mentoring prior K awardees and trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers value mentors with prior K award mentees and documented mentoring successes (e.g., Dr. Dowdy's mentoring record), which strengthens the application.
